input.extraction_context: import ZIP as new slot, later activation

expected.error_category: unsafe archive entry: Windows drive-absolute path

notes: D-006 correction, not oracle parity. MSC 1 only ever ran on macOS, so its shell-based unzip never had to reason about Windows path forms; createSlotFromZIP's own doc comment admits 'no structural validation is enforced here' (lines 1002-1006) regardless of platform. MSC 2's agent runs on Windows too (msc2-engineering.md platform matrix), and imported world ZIPs are exactly the kind of external, untrusted input D-006's 'correction' category exists for: a drive-absolute entry (C:\...) is a Windows-native escape from the target root that a Unix-only traversal/absolute-path check (looking only for a leading '/') would not catch. Phase 6's extractor rejects any entry that is drive-absolute or otherwise not a plain relative path, on every platform, regardless of which platform produced the archive.
